nodes.label: Rule: never touch the game
nodes.rationale: Tools may only read pixels (grim or a custom capture command) and the log file; no memory reading, no network traffic, no synthetic input to the game. This is the repo's core safety invariant.

nodes.label: Warden TypeScript is maintained, Rust deprecated
nodes.norm_label: warden typescript is maintained, rust deprecated
nodes.rationale: apps/warden/ts is the maintained version; the Rust source in apps/warden/src is kept only for its Windows window, must not be changed, and TypeScript tests need not match its output.

nodes.label: Bun workspaces layout (apps/* depend on packages/*)
nodes.norm_label: bun workspaces layout (apps/* depend on packages/*)
nodes.rationale: Apps depend on packages as workspace:* and packages MUST NOT import from apps, so shared code stays in one place and dependency direction is one-way. Adding a dashboard tool is one entry in packages/launch/src/tools.ts.

nodes.label: Arcana honest limits list
nodes.rationale: The README documents explicitly what the log cannot carry (board geometry, tile contents, which card is in hand, life total, exact chest rewards) so the tracker never pretends to know it; a solver would require screen capture and image recognition like the Tartarus helper, which is out of scope for this app.

nodes.label: Arcana log carries no board geometry
nodes.norm_label: arcana log carries no board geometry
nodes.rationale: Widget ids in the log are allocated as the game scrolls the board, so they say nothing about cell positions; the tracker reports only the shape of the walk and does not pretend to know the board. A Tarot Path solver would need screen capture, a different job from reading the log.

nodes.label: Why Warden was ported from Rust to TypeScript
nodes.norm_label: why warden was ported from rust to typescript
nodes.rationale: The monorepo is all TypeScript on Bun so tools can share code and run from one dashboard. The port was accepted when it matched the Rust state-for-state; the Rust source stays only for its Windows window and nothing keeps the two in step. The TS solver was ~5x slower than Rust, so the solve now runs in a worker so it does not block the screen.

nodes.label: Why shared packages exist
nodes.rationale: PNG decoding, window capture, running tesseract, and finding the game's log were each written twice (once per tool); they were factored into packages/* so there is one copy, while game-specific engines and random numbers deliberately stay in each app.

nodes.label: Silent grim capture policy on Niri
nodes.norm_label: silent grim capture policy on niri
nodes.rationale: Niri announces every window screenshot it takes itself with an un-dismissable notification, so @tli/capture uses only silent grim paths by default; --niri-screenshot or TLI_NIRI_SCREENSHOT=1 explicitly opts in to the announced path.

nodes.label: Chest-of-destiny loot attribution by timing
nodes.rationale: The log never says which item came out of which chest, so loot picked up just after a chest opens is attributed to that chest; this is right almost always but can misattribute when stage loot and chest loot are picked up close together. The tracker states this rather than hiding it.

nodes.label: Read-only policy (pixels and log only)
nodes.rationale: The tools are unofficial and unaffiliated; to stay safe and non-invasive they only read the game's pixels and log file, never memory, network traffic, or input; the only network fetch is the optional community price list (--no-baseline turns it off).

nodes.rationale: Transparent, pointer-events:none window (CSP default-src 'self') that only draws the numbered pulsing boxes and labels for the highlighted move; all behavior comes from mark.js.

nodes.label: Overlay card UI (overlay.html)
nodes.rationale: Draggable card (top bar is -webkit-app-region: drag, moved by Windows itself as Tartarus Overlay's card) with Snap/Helper/fold buttons, next move, alternatives, warnings, an updating progress line, and a debug-report send prompt; behavior in overlay.js.

nodes.label: Board analyzer page (analyze.html)
nodes.rationale: Board input via screenshot drop/paste, live game (log + window share), or manual entry; advice and deep check run entirely in the browser (vorax-engine.js + vorax-workers.js).

nodes.label: Card odds page (odds.html)
nodes.rationale: Ledger layout comparing each card's live share (Wilson 95% interval) with the simulator's assumed chance; verdict column flags cards the real game deals more or less often than simulated.

nodes.label: Vorax Helper Windows desktop app
nodes.rationale: npm start copies the helper pages from ../web into the app; same pages and advice as the web build. When the game runs as administrator Windows refuses window capture, so the app takes its own pictures of the game window or reads the screen with the card hidden.

nodes.label: Beak of the Twice-Born
nodes.rationale: Next-best advanced instrument for most builds, equal to Madonna with Incubation Sac, because it adds a monster every round (triggering the Sac).
nodes.source_location: Rules that apply to every run

nodes.label: Chrysalis Specimen
nodes.rationale: Only basic that rewards planning over round-by-round greed: weak until several Pest groups exist, then ~16% better when early rounds are spent building Pests.

nodes.label: Hypertrophic Pituitary
nodes.rationale: +80 Activity to a random monster every round, but only while you hold a Rare or Boss Agito, so the first goal is awakening a Rare Agito.

nodes.label: Incubation Sac
nodes.rationale: Strongest basic (1.22M ± 66k with Madonna): +45 Quantity to every monster on each add once you have 2+ Pest groups; pays off immediately. Keep an empty tank or two — a failed add (all 6 tanks full) does not trigger the Sac.

nodes.label: Plague Madonna
nodes.rationale: Best advanced instrument for every basic; take it whenever offered. With Agito it also raises the Agito's rarity.
nodes.source_location: Rules that apply to every run

nodes.label: Board sharing
nodes.rationale: On by default: read boards (tank numbers, card and instrument names, round — no pictures, names or accounts) are sent to the helper's maker to improve advice; users are told the first time and can turn it off (Share boards).

nodes.label: Move highlight
nodes.rationale: Numbered glowing boxes (1 card, 2 tanks, 3 Confirm) drawn over the game so the move can be played without reading; boxes are only drawn — clicks pass through and the reader never sees them. Hidden from round 11 (protocols) onward.

nodes.label: Problem reporting
nodes.rationale: Reports hold only the helper's own record of the latest run and no game-log text (UE_game.log is read only for 'board changed' moments); a scrubber blanks user/machine names before zipping; every send surface has a 'Look at the files first' preview and closing it sends nothing.

nodes.label: Terminal TUI (scripts/tui.ts)
nodes.rationale: Linux terminal version: same reader and advice, no overlay. The game log gates capture (no pictures while the board is closed); grim is used for silent capture because Niri's own screenshot always fires a notification; --capture-cmd supports other compositors; TLI_NO_CAPTURE=1 disables all pictures (used by the tests so they never touch the desktop).

nodes.label: Vorax Helper
nodes.rationale: Reads the board from the game window and advises; it only reads and advises and never clicks or types in the game. Runs as a Windows desktop app, in the browser, or as a Linux terminal TUI.

nodes.label: Deep check
nodes.rationale: Each option is followed by the rest of the run played by the validated strategy on the same random draws (30/60/150 playouts), ranked by chance of reaching the target; whiskers are the 95% range, and a wide whisker means more playouts are needed to separate close options.

nodes.label: Live vs simulator odds comparison
nodes.rationale: Where the simulator's chance falls outside the live Wilson 95% interval, the game shows the card more or less often than the simulator assumes — a direct calibration check on the advice engine's card odds.

nodes.label: Instrument picking playbook
nodes.rationale: Instruments are the biggest lever and the pick can't be redone (chosen at 8,000 and 28,000 Ultimate Activity thresholds), so refresh until a strong one shows; avoid Aberrant Stinger, Nettle Toggle and Two-Inch Skull Nail. Build tables with both instruments from round 1 are a ceiling, not a plan — always validate in dealt (realistic) mode, which is what this guide does.

nodes.label: Board collector Cloudflare Worker
nodes.rationale: Only board numbers and card names are stored — no pictures, log lines or IP address; boards are accepted only with the sender's KEY, while a separate EXPORT_KEY downloads them, so the sending key is safe to share with friends.

nodes.label: GitHub issues integration
nodes.rationale: Each report can also open a GitHub issue carrying the player's note, app version, screens/settings and the board — never the pictures, the log or anything about the player (the full report stays private in R2). Driven by a fine-grained GITHUB_TOKEN with Issues: Read and write; at most 20 issues a day; label 'player report'.

nodes.label: R2 bucket vorax-reports
nodes.rationale: Free R2 storage (10 GB ≈ 1,000 reports) holds player-sent debug bundles; limits 25 MB a report, 10/day per sender, 300/day total.

nodes.label: Reader recording
nodes.rationale: Everything the reader does is recorded locally (browser tab: last 40 pictures; desktop: last 5 runs under %APPDATA%\Vorax Helper\records) so a misread can be inspected exactly as it happened; nothing is uploaded automatically. Player hand-fixes are treated as ground truth the reader is checked against.

nodes.label: Optimal-play simulation methodology
nodes.rationale: Numbers come from the repo's own game engine driven by bots that never see the dice (unknown card order and random effect placement), judging cards by average result over many outcomes. Round-by-round play beat planning for every basic except Chrysalis Specimen (planning +16%), so each build uses its better style and so does the overlay. Scale: 208–400 games per build/style, 128,000 games for advanced-instrument ordering, 800 games for board-aware vs fixed picking. Caveats: simulator rules are best guesses; potion lists not re-checked with current bots; the planning bot's look-ahead is noisy.
